release: Downloads State Integrity & Smart Import Recovery
name: Downloads State Integrity & Smart Import Recovery
changes: Downloads Remaining, counts, speed, ETA, and queue presentation are derived from the same canonical visible job set used to render cards; raw SAB aggregate remaining is retained only for diagnostics.
Every live SAB Queue slot must produce a visible NewzDeck card. A slot that escapes normal ownership adoption is surfaced as a recovery/stopping card instead of remaining a hidden transfer.
NewzDeck's durable user Pause/Resume intent is the user-facing pause state. A raw internal SAB Paused condition is tracked separately and recovered by the background coordinator.
The Downloads footer reports an unexpected engine pause as recovery rather than falsely claiming the user paused the queue.
Smart Import claims validate their owning process PID. Imports orphaned by an update/service restart are reclaimed immediately rather than waiting for the historical lease to expire.
Smart Import writes a progress heartbeat; a live import with no progress heartbeat for 90 seconds is visibly marked IMPORT STALLED.
Diagnostics exposes raw-vs-visible remaining bytes, snapshot consistency corrections, engine-pause recovery, and dead-runtime import-reclaim counters.
regression_guards: User-facing Remaining can never be sourced solely from SAB aggregate remaining.
If visible Active/Queued/Retry/Stopping jobs are all zero, transfer Remaining is zero even if SAB returns an inconsistent aggregate byte count.
Every live SAB queue slot is represented before counts and Remaining are finalized.
A real user-requested Pause remains durable and immediate.
A live Smart Import owner PID retains its claim; only a dead owner is reclaimed automatically.
Import-stall detection does not start a duplicate import while the owner process is still alive.
v3.6.16 verified Remove/Cancel and Active-continuity protections remain preserved.
v3.6.15 Wanted-state reconciliation and v3.6.14 Automation JSON-save protections remain preserved.
